survey: Outdoor stone chess table with two round stools on a lawn. The table is one carved stone block: a thick square top with rounded edges and an inlaid navy-and-cream checkerboard, sitting on a pedestal that narrows at the waist and flares into a stepped square plinth. The plinth rests flat on the grass and casts a contact shadow. Each stool is a round seat on a waisted pillar with a ringed round base, sitting flat on the grass and shadowed, one front-left and one back-right of the table. The checkerboard faces up toward the camera at a three-quarter angle. All parts are solid stone with no joints, cables or moving parts. The weight is carried straight down through wide bases, so the set could stand. The stools are a sensible seat height for the table.

errors.where: Checkerboard inlay on the table top
errors.what: The grid does not seem to be 8×8. The board reads as roughly 6 rows by 8 columns, and the squares look stretched into rectangles, so it could not hold a real chess game. Everything else in the set stands and works.

fix: Inlay a standard square chessboard of 8 by 8 alternating navy and cream squares, all squares equal and square, centered on the stone table top with an even stone border on all four sides.
